correctness.rationale: For the stabilizer H of a proper 6A, put t=|H|. Kneser gives |6A| >= 6|A+H|-5t while properness gives |6A| <= p^a-t. Since |A|>(p-1)p^(a-1)/4, it follows that (p-3)p^(a-1)/2<4t. This contradicts t<=p^(a-1) for p>=11; at p=7 it forces H to be the kernel of reduction modulo 7 (also valid at a=1). The image of A then contains two distinct classes, whose sixfold sums cover the seven classes; H-periodicity lifts coverage to the entire group. The witness {1,2} is a strict majority of Q(7) and has only six fivefold sums. Coverage at any smaller order would imply coverage at order five by adding fixed terms. This is an analytic check for every a; the frozen Python tests are supplementary.

evidence: For d=p^b with d=1 mod 6 the contribution to chi-1 equals n/6-n/(6d); with d=5 mod 6 it equals n/6+n/(6d). Thus chi-1=(n-1)/6 for p=1 mod 6, and p^(a-1)(p+1)/6 for p=5 mod 6. Both are strictly below (p-1)p^(a-1)/4 for the relevant p>=7. In order seven every pair has at most six fivefold sums and {1,2} is an admissible pair of squares.

originality.rationale: The claimed covering theorem is an immediate specialization of the older exact unrestricted critical-number theorem. It holds without restricting A to squares and even at equality when half the square count is an integer. Sharpness of the uniform six is the elementary two-element obstruction in the group of order seven; the square restriction merely supplies a permissible pair.
